shadow_trades.reasoning_summary: I currently have equal amounts (1 each) of A, B, and C. Trading away my only A for a second B would leave me with 0 A and 2 B, reducing variety and utility. Since I value variety, this trade would not improve my bundle.
My current inventory is balanced (1 each), so trading away a B to get an extra A would create imbalance (2A/0B/1C), reducing variety value. This trade doesn't improve my utility.

Current bundle is balanced (1,1,1). Giving up my only B for 2 more A would leave me with 3 A, 0 B, 1 C - a highly imbalanced bundle that reduces variety, which I value. Better to seek trades that maintain or improve diversity.
Currently I have equal amounts (1 each) of A, B, C. Trading away my only C for another B would make me have 0 C and 2 B, reducing variety and utility. Not beneficial.

Trading 1B for 1C would just swap equal quantities (1 each currently), resulting in 0 B and 2 C, moving away from variety rather than toward it. This decreases my utility since I'd have an imbalanced bundle instead of my current even 1-1-1 spread.

Trading away my only B (going to 0) to get a second C would leave me with 1A, 0B, 3C - a very unbalanced bundle. Since I value variety, this would reduce utility rather than increase it. I'd rather keep balanced holdings.
This trade would leave me with 0 A and 2 B, reducing variety (1,1,1 is balanced). Since I value variety, trading away my only A for a second B decreases utility rather than increasing it.
I currently have equal amounts (1 each) of A, B, and C. This trade would give me 2 A and 0 B, creating imbalance and leaving me with nothing of B, which reduces variety utility. Not beneficial.

Current inventory is balanced (1,1,1). Trading away my only B for 2 more A would make me 3A/0B/1C, creating a large imbalance and leaving me with zero variety in B, which hurts my utility since I value variety. Better to seek a trade that keeps or improves balance.

I currently have equal amounts (1 each) of A, B, and C. Trading away my C for another B would leave me with 2 B and 0 C, reducing variety and utility rather than improving it. I'd rather keep balanced or trade to increase a good I have less of.
Trading away my only B for another C would leave me with 1A/0B/2C, reducing variety and utility since I already have equal amounts of all goods. This trade doesn't improve my bundle.

Current inventory is 1/1/1, perfectly balanced. Giving up my only B for 2 C would leave me with A:1, B:0, C:3, which is much less varied and thus lower utility under my preference for variety. Rejecting to seek a more balanced trade.
Currently I have 2 A, 0 B, 2 C - a very imbalanced bundle. Trading 1 A for 1 B moves me to 1 A, 1 B, 2 C, which is much more balanced and increases my utility given my preference for variety.

Giving up 2A for only 1B would leave me with 0A, 1B, 2C - reducing variety and giving away my scarce good at bad ratio. Trading 2A for just 1B is not favorable since I'd end with an even more imbalanced, and depleted, inventory of A. I'd prefer a 1-for-1 trade instead.

Currently I have 0 B and 2 C, so B is more valuable to me at the margin than C. Trading 1 C for 1 B moves me toward a more even distribution (A:2, B:1, C:1), which increases my utility given my preference for variety.

This trade would leave me with A:2, B:1, C:0, eliminating C entirely and creating a new imbalance. Giving up 2C for 1B is too steep - I'd rather trade 1-for-1 to gain variety without depleting a good completely. I'll propose a better ratio instead.

I currently have equal amounts (1 each) of A, B, and C. Trading away my only A for a second B would leave me with 0 A, 2 B, 1 C, reducing variety and utility since I'd lose a good entirely while doubling up on another. This doesn't improve my bundle.

This trade would move me from an even 1-1-1 bundle to 2A-0B-1C, increasing my holdings of A (already have) while eliminating B entirely, which reduces variety and thus utility. Not beneficial given my preference for balanced diversity.

Current inventory is 1/1/1, a balanced bundle I value for variety. Giving up my only B to get 2 more A would leave me with 3A/0B/1C, which is heavily skewed and loses the variety I value. The marginal value of extra A is low since I already have one, while losing B entirely removes a good. This trade decreases my utility, so I reject it.

I currently have equal quantities (1 each) of A, B, and C. Trading away my only C for another B would make me have 2 B and 0 C, reducing variety and utility. Since I value variety, this trade would not improve my bundle.

I currently have equal quantities (1 each) of A, B, and C. Trading away my B for C would leave me with 0 B and 2 C, creating imbalance and reducing variety value. This trade doesn't improve my utility since it just shifts equal holdings without net benefit.

Current inventory is 1/1/1, perfectly balanced. Trading away my only B for 2 C would give me 1 A, 0 B, 3 C — a much less diverse bundle, which is worse under my variety-preferring preferences even though total goods increase.

Trading A (3, abundant) for B (1, scarce) improves variety balance: post-trade I'd have A:2, B:2, C:1, which is more balanced than A:3, B:1, C:1. This increases my utility given my preference for variety.
I already have 3 A (my most abundant good) and only 1 B (my scarcest good). This trade would increase my A surplus further while depleting my only B, worsening variety and utility. Not favorable.

Giving 2A for 1B would drop me to A:1, B:2, C:1 - overcorrecting variety since A becomes scarce. A more balanced trade like 1A for 1B would be better. I'll reject this and propose a 1-for-1 swap instead.

I already have 3 A, the most of any good, and only 1 B. Giving up my only extra B to get more A would worsen my variety balance (going from B=1 to B=0 while A grows to 5). This decreases utility since I value diversity across goods.

Currently I have equal B and C (1 each), so trading C for B would just swap scarcity without improving variety—I'd still have 1 of each, but now 0 C and 2 B, actually making C=0 which is worse since I'd lose my only C. I prefer to keep at least one of each good, so I reject this trade to avoid losing my sole unit of C.

I currently have equal amounts of B and C (1 each), so trading away my only B for C would just swap scarcity without improving variety - I'd go from (B:1,C:1) to (B:0,C:2), making my bundle less balanced. I'd rather keep both or trade A, which I have more of.

Giving up my only unit of B would leave me with 0 B, which hurts variety badly, while I'd end up with 3 C - overly concentrated. Trading my last B for 2 C makes my bundle less balanced (3A,0B,3C) rather than more balanced. I'd prefer a trade that keeps some B or gives less C for something other than my sole B.

I currently have equal amounts (1 each) of A, B, and C. Trading away my only B for another A would leave me with 2 A and 0 B, reducing variety and utility rather than improving it.

Current inventory is 1/1/1, perfectly balanced. Trading 1C for 1B would just shift the imbalance to C=0, B=2, not improving variety - it's equivalent utility at best, no gain.

I currently have equal amounts (1 each) of A, B, and C. Trading away my only B for another C would make me have 0 B and 2 C, reducing variety and utility. Since I value variety, I should keep balanced holdings rather than swap one unit for another when I already have equal quantities.

Since I value variety, I want to increase my minimum holdings rather than trade my only unit of a good away. I'd prefer to keep A and acquire B without giving up my sole A, or get better terms.
Currently I have 0 B and 2 C, so trading a surplus C for a scarce B improves variety and balances my inventory to 1-1-1, increasing overall utility.

This trade would leave me with A:1, B:1, C:0, trading away all my C for just 1 B. Going from 2C to 0C while gaining only 1B is too costly - I'd end up with an empty category. A better trade would be giving only 1C for 1B, keeping some variety across all three goods.
This trade balances my inventory (A:2,B:1,C:1 -> A:1,B:2,C:1), moving toward a more even distribution which increases my utility given my preference for variety.
I already have 2 A and only 1 B and 1 C. Trading away my only B for another A would leave me with 3 A, 0 B, 1 C, making my bundle less balanced and reducing variety, which lowers my utility.

Current inventory: A:2, B:1, C:1. This trade would give me A:4, B:0, C:1 — losing my only B entirely and heavily overloading A, which hurts my variety-based utility. I'd rather keep balance across goods, so I reject this offer.
